legitimateExplanations.title: Persistent shortages on a lane.
legitimateExplanations.actually: A genuine count, labelling or system error at origin, or a units-of-measure mismatch between systems.
legitimateExplanations.ruleOut: Run a controlled count at origin and at destination for a defined period before treating the pattern as theft. Process error survives a controlled count; pilferage usually stops during it.

legitimateExplanations.title: Shortages concentrated on one driver.
legitimateExplanations.actually: That driver is simply assigned disproportionately to the affected lane or shift.
legitimateExplanations.ruleOut: Normalise by exposure. Compare shortages per movement or per consignment handled, never absolute counts, and test whether the lane or the individual is the better explanation.

legitimateExplanations.title: Losses concentrated on high-value items.
legitimateExplanations.actually: High-value items are more likely to be counted carefully and therefore more likely to have discrepancies detected at all.
legitimateExplanations.ruleOut: Compare detection rates as well as loss rates, and check whether low-value shortages are simply not being recorded.

countermeasures.text: Aggregate discrepancies continuously by route, driver, vehicle, transfer point, consignee and SKU class, and alert on sustained deviation from baseline rather than on individual events.
Establish process error or theft with a controlled count before any accusation, because this pattern has a genuinely high false-positive rate.
